name: card-fraud
title: Card fraud
summary: Approve, decline or challenge 2,000 card payments while fraud rings change tactics.

brief.goal: You are a card issuer's fraud model. One card payment arrives each turn, 2,000 in all, from a few hundred cards. Approve it, decline it, or step up (challenge the cardholder), and say how sure you are. About 1-4% are fraud, run by two to four rings that change tactics once, between turns 600 and 1,400. The truth comes late: a challenge resolves the next turn, anything else when its chargeback lands 30 to 50 turns later, in `feedback` and in `history`. You have 120 challenges.
brief.scoring: Out of 100, over resolved decisions. **Money, 60:** the fraud you stopped, minus 15% of each good payment you declined, minus 2-6 USD per challenge; approving everything earns 0, a perfect run 60. **Restraint, 20:** 10 × the share of challenges unused, plus 10 × (1 − false-decline rate ÷ 2%). **Confidence, 10:** 10 × (1 − 4 × Brier score). **Adapting, 10:** 10 × recall after the tactic change ÷ max(recall before it, 0.3); 0 if the match ends early. Each term is floored at 0 and capped at its points.
brief.ending: After 2,000 payments (completed). Early, as a failure, when the approved fraud charged back passes the loss cap: 12 × the fraud in the first 500 payments, and never under 75% of the match's fraud (loss-cap). Or when you decline more than 15% of the last 200 good payments resolved (decline-storm).
brief.reward: Each turn: the change in score, plus 0.02 when a challenge catches fraud and minus 0.02 when an approved fraud is charged back. The extras cancel on the last turn, so the rewards add up to the score.

inputs.name: payment
inputs.doc: The payment to decide this turn.

slices.name: amount
slices.doc: Its amount.

slices.name: category
slices.doc: The merchant's category.

slices.name: country
slices.doc: Where the merchant is, relative to the card's home country.

slices.name: channel
slices.doc: How the card was used.

slices.name: hour
slices.doc: Local hour of day.

slices.name: weekend
slices.doc: 1 on a Saturday or Sunday, else 0.

slices.name: ip_risk
slices.doc: Reputation of the payment's IP address: 0 clean to 1 known bad.

slices.name: cvv_match
slices.doc: Card security code: 1 matched, 0 mismatched, 0.5 not checked.

slices.name: avs_match
slices.doc: Billing address check: 1 matched, 0 mismatched, 0.5 not checked.

slices.name: merchant_risk
slices.doc: The merchant's past chargeback rate.

inputs.name: card
inputs.doc: This card's activity before this payment.

slices.name: since_last
slices.doc: Minutes since the card's previous payment; 43,200 (30 days) when it has none.

slices.name: payments_1h
slices.doc: Payments on the card in the last hour, counted up to 50.

slices.name: payments_24h
slices.doc: Payments on the card in the last 24 hours, counted up to 200.

slices.name: spend_24h
slices.doc: Amount spent on the card in the last 24 hours, counted up to 50,000.

slices.name: amount_ratio
slices.doc: This payment's amount ÷ the card's mean payment over 30 days (its usual amount when it has none).

slices.name: new_merchant
slices.doc: 1 if the card has never paid this merchant, else 0.

slices.name: new_country
slices.doc: 1 if the card has never been used in this country, else 0. Always 0 at home.

slices.name: device_cards
slices.doc: Cards seen on this payment's device in the last 7 days. 1 is a device only this card uses; 0 a device never seen.

slices.name: account_age
slices.doc: Days since the card was issued.

slices.name: your_declines_24h
slices.doc: Payments on this card you declined in the last 24 hours.

inputs.name: challenges_left
inputs.doc: Challenges you have left. A step-up with none left is a decline.

inputs.name: progress
inputs.doc: Share of the match played: 0 at the first payment, 0.9995 at the last.

inputs.name: history
inputs.doc: This card's previous 16 payments, newest first, including those from before the match. Rows past the card's history are all zeros, with `valid` 0.

columns.name: since_last
columns.doc: Minutes between it and the card's payment before it.

columns.name: decision
columns.doc: What was decided. Payments from before the match show approve.

columns.name: outcome
columns.doc: What it turned out to be, once known. Payments from before the match are good.

columns.name: valid
columns.doc: 1 for a real payment, 0 for an unused row.

inputs.name: feedback
inputs.doc: Truths that arrived this turn about your earlier decisions, on any card, newest decision first. At most 8 a turn; the rest wait for the next. Unused rows are all zeros, with `valid` 0.

columns.name: outcome
columns.doc: What it was: good or fraud, never unknown here.

columns.name: valid
columns.doc: 1 for a real row, 0 for an unused one.

outputs.name: decision
outputs.doc: What to do with this turn's payment.

codes.label: approve
codes.doc: Let it through. A fraud costs its full amount when its chargeback lands.

codes.label: decline
codes.doc: Refuse it. A good payment declined costs 15% of its amount.

codes.label: step-up
codes.doc: Challenge the cardholder: stops fraud, resolves next turn, uses one challenge and costs 2-6 USD. With none left, a decline.

outputs.name: confidence
outputs.doc: How likely your decision is right (a decline or step-up is right on fraud, an approve on a good payment). Scored by Brier score.

no_action: Approve, with confidence 0.5: the bank's stand-in rule when its model is silent. No payment is declined unseen and no challenge is spent.

stats.label: Score
stats.doc: The four terms in Scoring, added.

stats.label: Net money
stats.doc: Fraud stopped, minus 15% of the good payments declined, minus challenge costs.

stats.label: Recall
stats.doc: Share of the fraud you declined or challenged.

stats.label: False declines
stats.doc: Share of the good payments you declined.

stats.label: Brier score
stats.doc: Mean squared error of your confidence against whether the decision was right. 0.25 is a coin.

stats.label: Recall before the change
stats.doc: Recall on the fraud from before the rings changed tactics.

stats.label: Recall after the change
stats.doc: Recall on the fraud from after the rings changed tactics.

endings.label: Loss cap passed
endings.doc: Approved fraud charged back passed the loss cap.

endings.label: Decline storm
endings.doc: More than 15% of the last 200 good payments resolved were declined.

facts.label: Fraud rate
facts.doc: The seed's base share of fraud.

facts.label: Ring kinds
facts.doc: Which kinds of ring ran, as bits added: 1 card testing, 2 account takeover, 4 bust-out, 8 friendly fraud.

facts.label: Tactic change
facts.doc: The first payment, by turn, made with the new tactics.

codes.label: channel change
codes.doc: Online fraud moved to terminals and standing orders, and the reverse.

codes.label: new device per transaction
codes.doc: Card testing and takeovers use a fresh device every time.

codes.label: geography shift
codes.doc: Fraud moved into the card's home country, from cleaner IPs.

facts.label: Challenge cost
facts.doc: The friction cost of one challenge.

series.label: Net money
series.doc: Net money so far, over resolved decisions.

series.label: Fraud loss
series.doc: Approved fraud charged back so far.

series.label: False-decline loss
series.doc: 15% of the good payments declined so far.

series.label: Precision, last 100
series.doc: Over the last 100 resolved decisions, the share of your declines and challenges that were fraud. No sample until there is one.

series.label: Recall, last 100
series.doc: Over the last 100 resolved decisions, the share of fraud you declined or challenged. No sample until there is one.

events.label: Ring began
events.doc: A fraud ring made its first payment.

events.label: Chargeback
events.doc: An approved fraud was charged back.
